name: Bodrum
title: Holidays in Bodrum
intro: A crusader castle over a yacht-filled harbour, whitewashed houses and lively beach bays on Turkey's Aegean coast. Here's what Bodrum is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A stone windmill on a hill above Bodrum, with more windmills and the sea behind under a blue sky

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 2 hrs ahead of the UK (3 in winter)

facts.label: Entry
facts.value: No visa for up to 90 days

facts_note: Your passport needs at least 150 days left on it when you arrive. Check entry rules and the latest travel advice on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June, September and early October are the best times, hot and sunny with a warm sea. July and August are hot and busy, with a lively nightlife scene. The Aegean breeze keeps it a little cooler than the south coast. Winter is mild but quiet, and many hotels close.

things.name: Bodrum Castle
things.blurb: A castle built by the Knights of St John, home to the Museum of Underwater Archaeology.

things.name: Bodrum windmills
things.blurb: Old stone windmills on the hill between Bodrum and Gümbet, best at sunset.

things.name: Gulet boat trip
things.blurb: Day trips on traditional wooden boats stop at bays for swimming and lunch.

things.name: Gümüşlük
things.blurb: A fishing village with seafood restaurants on the water and the ruins of ancient Myndos.

things.name: Mausoleum of Halicarnassus
things.blurb: The site of one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, with a small museum.

things.name: Ephesus
things.blurb: Turkey's greatest Roman city is a long day trip away, about three hours each way.

faqs.question: Where is best to stay in Bodrum?
faqs.answer: Bodrum town is lively, with the castle and harbour. Gümbet is for nightlife. Yalıkavak, Türkbükü and Gümüşlük are quieter and more upmarket.

faqs.question: Is Bodrum good for beaches?
faqs.answer: The peninsula has lots of small bays with sun loungers and beach clubs rather than long sandy beaches.

faqs.question: How do you get to Bodrum from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly to Milas-Bodrum airport, about 40 minutes from town. There are direct flights from many UK airports in summer.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Bodrum?
faqs.answer: A week gives time for beaches, a boat trip and the castle. Add a few days for Ephesus.
